paper_metadata.title: A 1.2nJ/b 2.4GHz Receiver with a Sliding-IF Phaseto-Digital Converter for Wireless Personal/Body-Area Networks Yao-Hong Liu, Ao Ba, J.H.C van den Heuvel, Kathleen Philips, Guido Dolmans, Harmke de Groot

references.sentence: In this work, a single-channel sliding-IF RX with a phase-to-digital converter (SIF-PDC) is proposed, as illustrated in Fig. 9.5.1.
Figure 9.5.2 shows the phase-domain mathematical model of the SIF-PDC.
The implementation of the 4-b digital-to-phase converter (DPC) is shown in Fig. 9.5.3.
The measured time-domain waveform is shown in Fig. 9.5.4.
Figure 9.5.5 shows the measured raw bit-error-rate of a 2Mb/s HS-OQPSK signal with a pseudo-random bit stream.
Figure 9.5.6 summarizes and compares the performance with the state-of-theart ULP 2.4GHz RXs.
A die micrograph of the chip is shown in Fig. 9.5.7.

VLSI Circuits, pp. 148-149, June 2013. • 2014 IEEE International Solid-State Circuits Conference 978-1-4799-0920-9/14/$31.00 ©2014 IEEE Figure 9.5.1: Simplified block diagram of the proposed RX with SIF-PDC.
Figure 9.5.5: Measured bit error rate with 2Mb/s HS-OQPSK signal, adjacentchannel rejection and power breakdown of the presented RX.
ISSCC 2014 / February 11, 2014 / 10:45 AM 9 Figure 9.5.2: A phase-domain mathematical model of the presented SIF-PDC.
Figure 9.5.4: Measured time-domain demodulated waveforms of 2Mb/s HS-OQPSK and 1Mb/s GFSK signals.
Figure 9.5.6: Performance summary and comparison with the state-of-the-art low-power 2.4GHz RXs.
